chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah, from his father (peace be upon him), said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who prays the five [prayers] in congregation, so think good about him.'

key_terms.فَظُنُّوا بِهِ خَيْراً: So think good about him (positive assumption)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on judging those who pray in congregation?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on the merits of congregational prayer, this hadith links the outward act of communal worship (Salat al-Jama'ah) with the social virtue of positive judgment (husn al-zann). It serves as a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence for fostering communal harmony, suggesting that consistent public observance is a reliable indicator of piety and moral standing.
